To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

singular values of tensors exist and can be computed efficiently, that singular values of a tensor are invariant with respect to permutations of tensor indices and that the optimal low rank approximation of a tensor can be obtained by truncating its singular value decomposition.
the singular value decomposition can be extended to multilinear mappings, and the singular value decomposition of a tensor can be used to compute a low rank approximation of the tensor.

(i) singular values of tensors can be defined in a way that is consistent with the classical definition for matrices, (ii) these singular values are computable and have a clear algebraic interpretation in terms of the tensor’s multilinear map, (iii) the singular value decomposition can be applied to compute low-rank approximations of tensors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to generalize the classical concepts underlying the singular value decomposition to multilinear functions.
the question: What does it mean for a tensor to be of lower rank?
the question of how to extend the singular value decomposition from linear operators to higher order tensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the singular value decomposition of a tensor is the best approximation of the tensor by a sum of rank- one tensors, and the singular values are the best approximation factors.
the singular value decomposition of a tensor is the most powerful tool for the approximation of a given tensor by a low rank tensor.
the singular value decomposition and the singular value decomposition of a tensor are two different mathematical objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop an algebraic framework that is suitable for tensor decompositions.
the algebraic tools underlying the classical singular value decomposition can be generalized to arbitrary multilinear functions.
we provide an algebraic theory for the singular value decomposition of tensors, and a numerical theory for lower rank approximations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the singular values of a tensor are closely related to the eigenvalues of a nonnegative operator.

the algebraic concepts of singular values and singular vector decompositions can be generalized to arbitrary multilinear functions, and that this generalization is a powerful tool to solve approximation problems for tensors.
the singular values of a tensor can be computed in polynomial time.
